paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: how we treat people who are in need is how we treat Jesus. The King says, "whatever you did for one of the least of these brothers of Mine, you did for Me." (Matthew 25:40) Hungry, thirsty, a stranger, naked, sick, in prison: He names real needs, and He says He counts every answer to them as an answer to Him.

Now look at what surprised BOTH groups. The righteous ask, "Lord, when did we see You hungry and feed You…?" (Matthew 25:37) and the ones on the left ask, "Lord, when did we see You hungry or thirsty or a stranger or naked or sick or in prison, and did not minister to You?" (Matthew 25:44) I think nobody on either side was keeping score, and that's the point. The little everyday moments, a meal, a drink, a visit, were never little to Him.

So here's what I want you to carry out of my bakery. Ordinary kindness is not small, and ignoring someone in need is not small either, because the King says, "whatever you did not do for one of the least of these, you did not do for Me." (Matthew 25:45) Jesus lands this teaching with two places to go: "eternal punishment" or "eternal life." (Matthew 25:46) This is why my ovens stay ready, friend, and a ready baker keeps their eyes open for the next person who needs something. The teaching on the Mount of Olives wraps up here, so Jesus has now said all of it.
